newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO REVIEW BUDGET EXPENDITURES QUARTERLY.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO REVIEW BUDGET EXPENDITURES QUARTERLY.

text.p: Greece will initiate regular quarterly reviews of its budget expenditures from 1997 and study the restructuring of its foreign debt component in view of favourable economic developments, said Deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis.
"We will start reviewing budget expenditures at the end of every three month period to trace spending deviations and be able to intervene on time," Christodoulakis told reporters.

Greece was also studying ways to restructure its foreign debt, especially loans taken in the period 1994-95, to take advantage of lower risk premimums in international debt markets after the recent upgrading of its credit ceiling by Moody's, he added.
Greece has been refinancing outstanding loans denominated in foreign currencies carrying high interest rates.

Christodoulakis denied that the central bank's policy of keeping its overnight intervention rate steady over the last few months showed a disagreement with the finance ministry's aggressive rate cuts on its debt paper in the same period.
He said that the different pace of interest rate cuts between the finance ministry and the central bank reflected different reaction time horizons.

"Our goal is to reduce interest payments and extend the average maturity of public debt," said Christodoulakis. "The central bank's main concern is to combat inflation." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
